intro.title: Next.js App Router Fundamentals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple multi-page website using Next.js 13+ App Router to understand its file-based routing system. You'll learn how to create pages by adding React components to the `app` directory, where each folder automatically becomes a route. The core concept is dynamic routing, where you'll use special files like `page.js` and `layout.js` to structure your application. You'll work with React components, JSX, and Next.js-specific features to navigate between pages seamlessly. By the end, you'll have a functional site with multiple routes, demonstrating the fundamentals of the App Router.
intro.usecase: The Next.js App Router is the foundation for building modern web applications with complex navigation and data loading patterns. You'll see this in e-commerce platforms like Amazon where product pages, search results, and user dashboards are separate routes with different data requirements. Content-heavy sites like news portals or blogs use App Router features for dynamic routing to articles, category pages, and author profiles. Developers implement this pattern when building admin dashboards with nested layouts, authentication-protected routes, and server-side data fetching for real-time analytics.
